method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Background; states the preamble is not part of the order.
Establishes the objectives under Land Act s. 93.4 for FRPA purposes, applying to the landscape units of Map #1 and Table 1.
sections.gapNote: Code reads each Table 2 unit's landscape units from DataBC's RMP_LANDSCAPE_UNIT_SVW by LANDSCAPE_UNIT_PROVID, checking each record's name and emphasis option (mackenzieUnits.ts, mackenzieReads.ts). Review → Mackenzie old forest (oldForest/mackenzie.ts) calculates it as evidence beside the pack's margins, which stay the reviewer's answers. Which unit a block lies in is still the reviewer's to say.

sections.bearsOn: The objectives apply to all Crown land in the district except land under woodlot licences, research forests or community forest licences "that are 600 hectares or smaller".
sections.gapNote: Code leaves out land that is not provincial Crown, every woodlot licence (the CFLB definition names them without a size) and community forests whose whole licence is 600 ha or less; larger community forests (K2M, 26,302 ha) and TFLs stay (mackenzieReads.ts). Research forests are not read: no public layer of them was found. Reading the 600 ha as qualifying all three tenures would change only research forests here.

sections.bearsOn: Replaces the June 30, 2004 provincial non-spatial old growth order in the area covered.
sections.gapNote: Nothing to test beyond knowing which order governs Mackenzie old forest.

sections.bearsOn: Discloses a minor conflict with s. 1.A.g and Table 2 (old) of the 2002 Obo River and Fox landscape unit order and says this order applies where old forest retention is uncertain.
sections.gapNote: Matters only in the Obo River and Fox units; a rule would point the reviewer to this order's figures there.

sections.bearsOn: Bounds the landscape units the objectives are measured over (replaced by the January 2010 map).
sections.gapNote: Code reads DataBC's current landscape unit polygons, not the January 2010 map, which is not attached to the amendment as published; the units' names and emphasis options match Table 2.

sections.bearsOn: Defines the biodiversity emphasis option, BEC, community forest agreement area, deciduous species (birch or aspen), licensee and young forest (0-20 years).
Groups BEC variants into Groups 1-7 (and BWBS deciduous-leading as 6&7) for Objectives 2 and 3.
sections.gapNote: Code puts each VRI stand in its group (mackenzieUnits.ts): "ESSmv4" is read as ESSFmv4, and a later BEC label that dropped a variant number (BWBSdk, BWBSmw, ESSFmvp, ESSFwcp) stands for the Table 1 variants it begins only where they all lie in one group. Group 1 and unlisted variants have no row and are reported, never counted.

sections.bearsOn: Defines the CFLB, the denominator of Objective 2, excluding private, federal, municipal land and woodlots.
sections.gapNote: Code uses the VRI proxy (treed on the forest management land base) on the ground 1.2 and this definition leave in; parks stay in it (mackenzie.ts).

sections.bearsOn: Defines NFAs as unharvested beetle-affected stands that may count toward the old forest target.
sections.gapNote: Code splits old forest by age into live and dead by the VRI's STAND_PERCENTAGE_DEAD; the dead part is the NFA counted. Young natural forest is not counted as NFA.

sections.bearsOn: Old forest is >120 years in SBSmk1 and SBSmk2, >100 years in BWBS deciduous-leading stands, and >140 years elsewhere.
sections.gapNote: Code applies it stand by stand (mackenzieOldFrom): from 121 in SBSmk1 and SBSmk2, from 101 in BWBS stands led by birch or aspen, from 141 elsewhere.

sections.bearsOn: Old forest must be maintained on the CFLB of each landscape unit (or group) and BEC group at no less than the Table 2 minimum, subject to (a)-(d).
sections.gapNote: Code calculates every Table 2 row of a unit for every schedule and period (mackenzie.ts). Review → Mackenzie old forest (oldForest/mackenzie.ts) calculates it as evidence beside the pack's margins, which stay the reviewer's answers.

sections.bearsOn: NFA may make up the old forest target, but its share cannot exceed the share of the area affected by the epidemic or catastrophic event.
sections.gapNote: Code caps the NFA counted at the affected share the reviewer states (no default; without one, all old forest by age counts). No layer gives the affected share.

sections.bearsOn: Of the live old forest portion of the target, up to 20% may come from stands younger than old where equal or better conservation benefits are shown; unlike PG TSA D.4 it does not extend to interior.
sections.gapNote: The rule tests the younger-stand share the reviewer enters; the calculation, when the reviewer switches it on with an age and the benefit, counts younger stands toward at most 20% of the target less the NFA counted, never toward interior, and shows the share as evidence.

sections.bearsOn: Where beetle harvest or wildfire removed retention opportunities, the stands closest to old age must be identified and maintained to reach Objective 2 soonest.
sections.gapNote: Not modelled; a rule like PG D.5(a) would ask whether a deficit exists and whether recruitment stands are identified.
proposedFacts: Has beetle harvest or wildfire eliminated opportunities to meet the old forest target in this unit?
Have the stands closest to old age been identified and kept out of the schedule?

sections.bearsOn: Heather Dina Lake, Muscovite Lakes and Ed Bird Estella Lake parks may count toward the targets of Parsnip, Blackwater and Buffalohead.
sections.gapNote: Code lets the reviewer join Muscovite Lakes and Ed Bird Estella Lake parks (DataBC's own landscape unit polygons) to Blackwater and Buffalohead; off by default. After the 2010 amendment Parsnip is no longer in Table 2, so Heather Dina Lake Park has no target left.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of CFLB retained as old forest by landscape unit (group), BEO and BEC group (9-28%); repealed and replaced by the 2010 amendment.
sections.gapNote: Repealed; kept as data (mackenzie-2008-biodiversity-order.json) only to check the 2010 table's transcription, which equals it less the seven groups (mackenzie.test.ts).

sections.bearsOn: A percentage of the old forest requirement must be old interior forest per Table 3, subject to (a) and (b).
sections.gapNote: Rules take the reviewer’s old and old interior margins. Review → Mackenzie old forest (oldForest/mackenzie.ts) calculates it as evidence beside the pack's margins, which stay the reviewer's answers. Interior follows Guidance 4 with lakes and reservoirs buffered.

sections.bearsOn: Where beetle harvest or wildfire eliminated interior retention, the stands closest to old age must be identified and maintained.
sections.gapNote: As 2(c), for interior.
proposedFacts: Have stands closest to old age been identified to recruit old interior forest where beetle harvest or fire removed it?

sections.bearsOn: The same three parks may count toward the old interior targets.
sections.gapNote: As 2(d): the park joins its unit's interior when the reviewer switches it on.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of old forest retention that must be interior, by BEC group and BEO (10-50%).
sections.gapNote: Code sets each row's interior share from Table 3 by its groups and emphasis option. Two rows are left open: Upper Ospika's "2, 3" (25% or 50% at High) and Philip, Philip Lake, Tudyah A, printed "Low / Intermediate" (10% or 25%). Its heading's "Table 1" is read as Table 2.

sections.bearsOn: Takes effect on Gazette publication.
Does not affect Category A cutblocks approved under the FPC on or before the effective date.
sections.gapNote: Rare now; a transition question as in the PG pack would do.

sections.bearsOn: Despite FRPA s. 16(2), every FSP submitted after the effective date must be consistent with the order.
sections.gapNote: No FSP check for Mackenzie old forest objectives.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the FRPA s. 8(2)(b) period at one year for FSPs to be amended to the new objectives.
sections.gapNote: Period long expired.

sections.bearsOn: States the guidance is not legally binding.
NFAs stand in for live old forest, chosen by remnant live patches, partly killed stands and snag-bearing stands; a representative live portion in proportion to the unaffected area may be kept.
sections.gapNote: Guidance to Objective 2(a); see that gap.

sections.bearsOn: Spatial OGMAs are to be developed in priority landscape units roughly equal to the Table 2 and 3 amounts (done for seven units in the 2010 spatial order).
sections.gapNote: Legal OGMAs are already shown by the ogma screen.

sections.bearsOn: Small landscape units are grouped in Table 2 so targets are met over the group, with retention expected to be distributed across the grouped units.
sections.gapNote: Grouping is part of the Table 2 gap; distribution across grouped units is a reviewer judgement.

sections.bearsOn: Suggests computing old interior forest as old forest or NFA at least 200 m from younger stands (200 m from pine/deciduous NSR or age class 1-3 and other NSR or 1-4), and from lakes, primary roads, pipelines, railways and hydro corridors, but not secondary roads.
sections.gapNote: Code follows the table and buffers lakes and reservoirs (VRI BCLCS_LEVEL_5 LA and RE), FSRs, railways, transmission lines and pipelines by 200 m, patch by patch (mackenzie.ts).

sections.bearsOn: Small BEC units are merged into other groups; a proposal may combine BEC group targets across units with under 2,000 ha of CFLB; Group 1 is left out of Objective 2 because large harvest is not expected there.
sections.gapNote: Group 1 (parkland and alpine variants) has no target; the calculation reports CFLB no row holds and never counts it. Combining small groups is a proposal to the minister's designate, not modelled.

sections.bearsOn: Ten named landscape units are to be managed as LRMP Wildlands, which exclude commercial timber harvesting; the guidance says this part of the LRMP is guidance, not legal.
sections.gapNote: A rule asks whether the block is in a wildlands landscape unit; no screen maps those units.

sections.bearsOn: Assigns FSP preparation to licensees and BCTS, approval and enforcement to Forests.
Review with the Mackenzie TSR and a coordination group.
